name: United States (federal FLSA baseline)

minors.schoolDays: Mon-Fri outside summer, unless the org supplies a school calendar

restrictedPositions.note: 29 CFR 570.34(l): 15-year-olds may work as lifeguards at traditional swimming pools when certified; 14-year-olds may not.

leave.note: Family and Medical Leave Act: up to 12 weeks of unpaid, job-protected leave in a 12-month period for covered employers (50+ employees). Not yet verified against the official source.

cobra.note: Federal COBRA: group health plans of employers with 20+ employees; the employer tells the plan administrator within 30 days of the qualifying event, and the administrator sends the election notice within 14 days. Many states have their own continuation laws for smaller employers. Not yet verified against the official source.

aca.note: ACA: 130 hours in a month counts as full-time for the monthly measurement method. Not yet verified against the official source.

retention.note: Form I-9: 3 years after hire or 1 year after employment ends, whichever is later.
Employment tax records (W-4 and the like): at least 4 years.
Payroll records under the FLSA: 3 years.

notes: Federal floor only. States and cities may be stricter; mergeRules keeps the strictest value.

source.title: 29 CFR 570.35 - Hours of work for 14- and 15-year-olds
